# Independent performance review — round 2

Verdict: **PASS for the frozen static scope**. Both blocking round-1 P2 findings are resolved. This is not a runtime performance pass, task completion, IDE completion or generated-tree parity claim.

Reviewed worktree `/workspace/android-studio-source-providers`, base `ac58815bb268d338bea40a31fff630734cd719f4`, against `review-source-snapshot-round2.json`. Current SHA-256 identities:

- generated_artifacts.rs: c9981efb5b17c831e6c5dbdad47653d31fba74908772250d592e495c58aeb47b
- project_model.gradle: 508ecc9987932f8d184983f551eca0cb1bc9efa6ed12806dcaff8a0a2f6880b7
- tests/generated_artifacts.rs: 89c1fdbceecca43a00245ee2215b8c7e05b7fe0d49df0ac259047345aa2c155a

All 8 frozen source/data identities, all 184 immutable original guards, 31 cited reference hashes and 11 historical planning-probe hashes matched. End-of-review source/original hashes matched again. Prior FAIL report remains byte-identical at SHA 7c06b98082d3e3a291eab77adcba8e21ae47f3efdf8b08858d0dfbd37d4f2ef9. The 27 declared tests were read, not executed.

## Resolution of the blocking findings

1. **Quadratic module validation: resolved.** generated_artifacts.rs:457–472 still validates exact ordered module/directory correspondence and equal lengths before the zip at473. The subsequent per-module loop consumes the paired expected identity directly at559. It no longer searches the entire Basic identity list for each module. Module pairing is O(M), replacing the former O(M²) name comparisons. Zip cannot truncate away a trailing mismatch because the earlier equality check rejects unequal lists. Existing module and variant contradiction checks, JVM filtering and raw variant encounter preservation remain in force. A future multi-module regression covering reorder/missing/extra modules would be useful coverage; this recommendation is not a current blocker, and no existing test was removed or weakened to obtain this verdict.
2. **Redundant Basic JSON tree: resolved.** GeneratedRecord at373–386 declares only generatedArtifacts. Ordinary derived Serde handling skips unrelated top-level fields rather than retaining their contents as serde_json::Value. At418 the decoder parses that small envelope, then at424 moves the owned sidecar Value and at445 consumes it into GeneratedExport; there is no deep sidecar clone or unrelated Basic Value tree held throughout validation. The present_sidecar hook preserves present-null versus absent distinction, so missing metadata handling is not traded for allocation reduction. The new 600,000-character unrelated-payload regression at tests:754–761 asserts unchanged decoded artifact facts. That is a meaningful compatibility regression, not an allocation benchmark or proof of measured RSS. The no-unrelated-tree conclusion comes from the declaration and decode path inspected here.

## Revised static cost and behavior

For M Android modules, the exact identity comparison and paired validation are now linear in module count, plus identity/path/variant text length. Per-module variant/model/map duplicate checks use borrowed BTreeSet keys and take O(N log N) comparisons for each relevant collection; raw path lists are neither sorted nor deduplicated. Remaining model_producer/minimum-consumer lookups scan only each module's Versions entries, rather than searching across modules. Field/path traversal remains linear in total text and collection contents, apart from those ordered-set uniqueness checks.

The parser still scans Gradle output to locate exactly one record, checks its byte length at412–417 before JSON allocation, validates schema before DTO conversion and moves owned export modules into the snapshot. It allocates only the sidecar JSON/DTO and retained Basic identity data from this decode path. The JVM and caller still retain their own data; no hard 16 MiB memory guarantee is established. The sidecar uses an intermediate Value before conversion, which can have more overhead than its encoded bytes. No absolute peak RSS or elapsed-time figure is claimed.

Normalized path validation at606 builds one temporary normalized PathBuf per path, compares its exact bytes, then checks components and control characters. This preserves the added correctness contract without IO; its allocation is proportional to the current path length and does not retain a second copy of every path across the full model. No source discovery, Kotlin inference, rendering, startup hook or filesystem scan is introduced on the Rust side.

Bridge null/type guards at project_model.gradle:308/313–320 validate collections/maps without cloning or collecting them twice. The subsequent collect preserves emitted order and duplicate path encounters. Java-only task notApplicable validation remains a constant-size check per artifact. Per-module collection continues under the owner's project task lock and final aggregation follows the sorted Basic module list rather than ConcurrentHashMap iteration.

## Remaining advisory observations and runtime boundary

- Duplicate SDK construction is unchanged and remains **advisory, unmeasured**. Ordinary Android modules make new Versions/BasicAndroidProject/AndroidProject buildAll requests at project_model.gradle:306/341/344 alongside existing Versions/BasicAndroidProject requests at191/194. Pinned ModelBuilder dispatch/build code verifies that these are constructor calls; do not assume the duplicate requests are free. A later per-module query cache must preserve independent failure capture and usable Basic data. No runtime observation currently justifies escalating this to a blocker.
- File.canonicalPath is still called for emitted SDK paths. It can perform JVM filesystem work. Maintain the established canonical-path contract and raw collection duplicates; profile before adding a cache or changing behavior.
- ensure_current at313–317 still clones all identity strings/vectors for a same-revision comparison via model_identity at354–370. There are no product call sites yet. A future controller should validate once at publication or compare borrowed identities before invoking this method per row or frame. Stale revision/root checks already short-circuit.
- The 16 MiB record limit is a wire-input decoding limit, not a cap on total allocator use, process RSS, Gradle stdout buffering or JVM serialization. The new unrelated-data regression is not a performance measurement.
- Actual full AndroidTools tests, strict repository Clippy/format checks, fresh matching bridge SDK probes, and combined app build/native/full-CI gates remain pending the lead's exclusive leases. Historical probes are not current gates. An actual timing/RSS claim must identify the matching source, process, workload, measurement and cleanup separately.

No Cargo, Gradle, app, benchmark or cache operation was run. No product source, test, fixture, canonical matrix or protected branch was changed. Suggested .rules additions: none.
